prompts.A:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Original transparent game sprite atlas for a bright blue aquatic learning game for children ages 6–7.
Create a finished RGBA PNG image with a genuinely transparent background, exactly 1536 pixels wide and 1024 pixels high, landscape 3:2. The full canvas is an invisible 8-column by 6-row arrangement of equal cells (192 wide, about 170.7 high), no visible grid. Exactly ONE isolated complete creature per occupied cell. Every sprite fully fits inside its own cell with at least 18px transparent padding on all four sides, centered, entirely separated from adjacent sprites, no loose pixels outside its cell. Every creature looks RIGHT in friendly side or three-quarter profile. Never include left-facing creatures. Use varied identifiable anatomy and silhouettes, never substitute generic fish for distinct species.
Style: consistent polished soft 3D cartoon toy-like creatures, plump rounded forms, friendly curious large glossy eyes, cheerful age-appropriate appearance, soft dimensional shading inside each silhouette, clean dark blue contour, saturated bright colors with lighter creamy highlights. All are simple self-contained game sprites, no scene or environmental objects.
Constraints: transparent background and spaces between sprites, no ground shadows, no glow spreading outside silhouette, no text, no numbers, no labels, no watermark, no grid, no decorative bubbles or plants. No gore, no menace, no teeth emphasized, no scary face.
Layout must strictly follow the following row-major sequence, eight subjects per row, left to right:
ROW 1: (1) plankton as a tiny green translucent rounded micro-creature; (2) fish egg as a translucent amber egg with tiny visible embryo and eye; (3) fish fry as tiny pale baby fish; (4) tadpole with rounded head and long thin tail; (5) brine shrimp with elongated many-legged tiny crustacean body; (6) water flea with transparent oval shell and visible eye; (7) mosquito larva as slender segmented wriggler with tiny head; (8) tiny shrimp with curved pink body and antennae.
ROW 2: (1) silver minnow with sleek silver body; (2) guppy with colorful broad fan tail; (3) zebrafish with horizontal navy stripes; (4) cardinal tetra with full-length blue upper and red lower stripes; (5) neon tetra with bright blue stripe and red rear half; (6) mosquitofish with plain gray rounded small body; (7) medaka as small cream-orange ricefish; (8) goldfish with orange plump body and flowing fan tail.
ROW 3: (1) betta with vivid blue-red large flowing fins; (2) molly with black velvety body and round belly; (3) pearl gourami with spotted pale body and threadlike pelvic feelers; (4) cory catfish with armored stocky body and whiskers; (5) small tetra with silvery orange-accented tetra body; (6) bitterling with silvery iridescent pink-purple side; (7) topmouth gudgeon with upward mouth and dark side stripe; (8) small crucian carp with compact bronze oval body.
ROW 4: (1) tilapia fry with tiny pink-gray striped baby body; (2) loach with long bronze striped eel-like body and tiny whiskers; (3) yellow croaker with yellow-gold elongated body; (4) sardine with silver blue-backed streamlined body; (5) anchovy with extra slender silver body; (6) whitebait with translucent ivory tiny fish body; (7) baby octopus with round lilac head and eight short arms; (8) baby cuttlefish with cream rounded mantle and little frill.
ROW 5: (1) jellyfish with peach-pink dome and trailing soft tentacles; (2) seahorse with curved long snout and curled tail; (3) starfish with five friendly coral-orange arms; (4) crucian carp with bronze oval body; (5) carp with plump golden body and whiskers; (6) grass carp with long olive body; (7) silver carp with silver deep body and small eyes; (8) bighead carp with obvious large rounded head and speckled side.
ROW 6: (1) catfish with broad whiskered head and smooth blue-gray body; (2) snakehead with long patterned olive body and large snake-like head; (3) sea bass with robust silver-green body; (4) mandarinfish with chunky gold body, brown irregular mottled markings and spiny dorsal; (5) tilapia with deep oval lilac-gray striped body; (6) pomfret with broad silver diamond body; (7) hairtail with long thin metallic ribbon body gently curled to fit inside cell; (8) Spanish mackerel with sleek blue silver spotted body and forked tail.
The ordering is mandatory, with exactly 48 creatures in the specified 8 by 6 layout.

prompts.C:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Original transparent snake skin/head sprite atlas for a bright blue child-friendly game, ages 6–7.
Create a finished RGBA PNG with genuinely transparent background, exactly 1536x1024 pixels, landscape 3:2. Arrange exactly 16 isolated sprites in an invisible 8-column by 2-row grid. Each cell is exactly 192x512 px. Center each sprite in its cell, with abundant transparent padding; each sprite maximum 145px wide and 180px tall. No grid or labels. TOP ROW: exactly eight right-facing whole cartoon snake HEAD sprites, heads and a very short rounded neck only, compact three-quarter side profile with big friendly glossy eyes, closed smiling mouth, no tongues, no fangs. Do not show full snake bodies. BOTTOM ROW: exactly eight matching round snake BODY SEGMENT sprites, each a simple approximately circular 120px diameter softly dimensional body piece, no head, no face, no eye, no tail, no limbs. Match each body segment's species color/pattern to the head immediately above it. The body segments will form a chain in a game.
Species order LEFT TO RIGHT in both rows:
Column 1 corn snake: orange-red ground color with red saddle blotches and cream edges.
Column 2 green tree python: vivid leaf green with small white speckles and pale cream underside.
Column 3 ball python: chocolate brown/black with tan-gold rounded patch markings and cream underside.
Column 4 milk snake: glossy repeating red, cream and black bands.
Column 5 kingsnake: deep black with slender cream-white crossbands.
Column 6 garter snake: olive green with three clear bright yellow longitudinal stripes.
Column 7 rainbow boa: copper orange/brown with dark rings and gentle iridescent rainbow sheen.
Column 8 sea snake: soft blue-gray with broad dark navy bands and pale cream underside.
Style: polished original soft 3D cartoon toy-like sprites, plump rounded forms, soft dimensional shading inside silhouette, clear clean dark blue contour, cheerful saturated bright palette and pale highlights. Heads all face RIGHT. Evenly spaced self-contained sprites, crisp cutout silhouettes.
Constraints: keep each item fully within cell; transparent canvas and spaces; no shadows outside silhouette; no glow outside silhouette; no text, no letters, no numbers, no grid, no watermark, no background, no environmental objects. No scary expression, violence, tongues or sharp fangs. Exactly 8 heads on upper row and their 8 matching round body segments on lower row.
prompts.D:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Original transparent vocabulary card illustration sprite atlas for a bright blue adventure learning game for children ages 6–7.
Create a finished RGBA PNG image with genuinely transparent background, exactly 1536 pixels wide and 1024 pixels high, landscape 3:2. Arrange exactly 16 isolated complete objects in an invisible 4-column by 4-row grid of equal cells, each exactly 384px wide and 256px high. One whole object per cell, centered, all objects fit completely within their cell with at least 30px transparent padding all around. Strong visible separation. No card boxes, no background, no grid.
Style: consistent original polished soft 3D cartoon toy-like objects, plump rounded forms, friendly cheerful age-appropriate appearance, soft dimensional shading inside silhouette, clean dark blue outline, saturated bright colors and creamy highlights. Identifiable varied silhouettes. Crisp game asset cutouts suitable for English word cards. Same lighting and scale family across atlas.
Required row-major order, left to right:
ROW 1: tree, flower, leaf, grass. Tree has a clear entire trunk and rounded lush green canopy; flower is one complete pink/orange blossom with stem and two leaves; leaf is one complete bright green leaf with visible central vein; grass is one compact clump of several green blades with visible bases, no dirt ground.
ROW 2: seed, rose, cactus, bush. Seed is a large single golden-brown bean seed with recognizable seam; rose is a red rose bloom on short green stem with leaves; cactus is a plump green branching saguaro cactus with friendly rounded arms and tiny soft dot spines, no pot; bush is a compact rounded multi-lobed green shrub with tiny colorful berries, no scenery.
ROW 3: bus, car, boat, plane. Bus is a bright yellow friendly toy bus in three-quarter view; car is a rounded red toy car; boat is a blue and white small sailboat with mast and triangular sail; plane is a bright sky-blue friendly toy propeller airplane with wings and tail. Vehicles face RIGHT where directional. Each entire object fits cell.
ROW 4: cup, bed, clock, shoe. Cup is a pale peach mug with blue handle and visible rim; bed is a little single bed with aqua blanket, yellow pillow, wooden headboard and footboard; clock is a round cream-and-orange toy alarm clock with two small bells and simple dark hands but no numbers; shoe is a complete bright purple-blue child's sneaker facing RIGHT with soft laces.
Constraints: exactly 16 standalone objects in exact requested cell order; genuine alpha transparency; no outside silhouette shadows or glow; no text, no letters, no numerals, no watermarks, no card boundaries, no grid, no background scenes, no additional objects. All objects complete and individually isolated.
